statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 17% (low), Stress 43% (moderate), Confidence 87% (high). Shared assessment for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail returns to the low band, so the mapped state is EA_ON. The step down from the previous hour rests on specific observed evidence: the Nasdaq-100 set a fresh intraday record at 30,699.00 and was rejected there, and both the cash index and NQ futures now sit roughly 60 to 65 points below their session highs without reclaiming them. That is the second genuine two-way test of the session, after the opening dip to 30,496.43 was bought. The advance is also narrow rather than broad, with the S&P 500 at +0.02% against the Nasdaq-100 at +0.51%, application and infrastructure software lower while semiconductors lead, and the eight tracked megacaps split five up and three down. Cross-asset confirmation has decayed as well, with Treasury yields now flat to marginally higher rather than falling together and crude recovered from its earlier lows, while the volatility index sits at a 14.34 session low. Conditional risk is concentrated in a narrow 17:00-20:00 UTC band covering the 2-year note auction with Barkin and the power hour that carried Monday's highest reading, which is published as the danger window instead of a session-wide caution. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping. The reading would move back toward the watch and block bands on a reclaim of 30,699.00 cash that holds, shallow pullbacks that are each bought without meaningful retracement, repeated extension after failed retracements, or the index holding a session extreme while yields, the volatility index, crude, semiconductors, megacaps and breadth all confirm one direction.
headline: The Nasdaq-100 set a fresh intraday record at 30,699.00 and was rejected there, leaving both the cash index and NQ futures some 60 to 65 points below their session highs while the S&P 500 sits flat and software lags semiconductors; the observed retracement and narrow, rotating leadership return Tail to the low band
body: Tuesday's U.S. cash session has now produced its second two-way test, and that is the reason this assessment steps back down from the previous hour. What is observed. The Nasdaq-100 cash index trades at 30,638.80, up 156.45 points or 0.51%, inside a 30,496.43-30,699.00 range against Monday's record 30,482.35 close. The 30,699.00 print is a fresh intraday record, but the index now sits roughly 60 points beneath it and the high has not been reclaimed. NQ Dec-26 futures trade at 30,931.75, up 147.00 points or 0.48%, inside a 30,670.00-30,997.00 range, which places the contract about 65 points under its own session high. An hour ago the same two instruments were 19 points and 28 points from their highs respectively; that extreme-holding condition, which was the specific evidence behind the previous Tail of 21, has resolved into a rejection. Why the advance is not treated as one-way structure. The move is narrow rather than broad. The S&P 500 is 7,766.10, up 1.40 points or 0.02%, inside a 7,760.22-7,782.19 range and likewise off its high, and contemporaneous reporting describes the Dow as lower. The PHLX Semiconductor Index is 12,554.95, up 0.98% against a 12,433.17 close, but it too is about 46 points below its 12,600.74 session high. Shared cross-asset context collected at 15:12 UTC shows the same split internally: semiconductors up 0.83% and semiconductor equipment up 0.38% against application software down 0.48% and infrastructure software down 0.79%, with the eight tracked megacaps divided five up and three down, Microsoft down 1.22% and Amazon down 1.11% capping the index while Apple, Alphabet and Meta carry it. That context is delayed, latest-session data and is used only as confirmation of the rotational split visible in the independently fetched index levels, never as live price-path evidence. Rotation of this kind is the opposite of the broad, aligned participation that produces a path denying mean reversion. Cross-asset alignment has also decayed since the previous hour. Treasury yields are no longer falling: the 2-year is 4.75% and fractionally lower, the 5-year 4.83% and fractionally higher, the 10-year 4.96% and about half a basis point higher, the 30-year 5.30% and about a basis point higher. An hour ago all of 2Y, 5Y and 10Y were lower together. WTI is 91.30 dollars, down 1.16%, and Brent 99.92 dollars, down 0.42%, both still on a fifth consecutive lower session at a two-week low but both recovered from the steeper declines recorded earlier. The VIX is 14.34, down 3.56% from a 14.87 close and at its 14.34 session low. A falling volatility index alongside a rejected high, a flat broad market and flat yields describes an orderly, two-sided tape. Verified evidence gathered this run. The Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond's Fifth District manufacturing survey for September was confirmed at the primary source: the composite index fell to -2 from 4, with shipments at -5 from 11, new orders at -6 from 3, local business conditions at -6 from 4, and employment the only improving component at 7 from -2. The release also notes that the average growth rate of prices paid increased notably in September, a combination of softening activity and firmer input costs that is a genuine complication for a central bank that has recently resumed raising rates. Separately, President Trump addressed the United Nations General Assembly, scheduled for approximately 13:45 UTC, and his Iran remarks were reported at about 14:51 UTC, after the previous assessment was published. He framed a binary between a deal that lets Iran rebuild and rapid military escalation, and predicted a deal after the midterm elections. The observable market reaction was a further decline in crude to a two-week low on diplomatic hopes rather than an escalation premium, so this is treated as a resolved two-way headline that did not produce directional equity stress. What would change the reading. The reading moves back toward the watch and block bands on a reclaim of 30,699.00 cash that holds, a sequence of shallow pullbacks that are each bought without a meaningful retracement, repeated extension after failed retracements, or the index holding a session extreme while yields, the volatility index, crude, semiconductors, megacaps and breadth all confirm a single direction. None of those conditions is present. Scheduled risk ahead. The 69 billion dollar 2-year note auction and Barkin remarks fall together at 17:00 UTC, and the power hour from 19:00 UTC carried Monday's highest published Tail reading. Those two checkpoints define the published 17:00-20:00 UTC danger window, which is preferred to a broader session-wide caution. Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC, landing fifteen minutes after the cash open, are the highest-impact release in the forward calendar and drive the step up in the final two forecast hours. A Trump-Xi summit is reported for Thursday, but no exact time could be verified, so it is deliberately omitted from the structured event list rather than published with a guessed timestamp and is carried instead as a checkpoint in the hourly drivers. Source notes. Several live market blogs consulted for this run returned bot-block responses rather than content: Reuters, CNBC, MarketWatch and CNN were each unavailable, which is a site-level restriction and not a research gap in the underlying numbers, all of which were obtained from quote and primary sources directly. The shared Finviz context was fresh at thirteen minutes old but its collection status is partial, with the calendar and futures sections both unavailable; only the breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections were usable and they are used solely as confirmation. One quote-page field is internally inconsistent and has therefore not been relied upon or published: the futures page lists a previous settlement that cannot be reconciled with its own reported point and percentage change, so the change figures and the settlement reference verified in the previous hour were used instead. The dominant mode is mixed: an index-level advance to a fresh record high, but with a two-way intraday path and materially split internals. Stress at 43 reflects the record-high starting point, the narrow and rotating leadership, the contractionary regional survey with firmer prices paid, the pending front-end auction and the unresolved Iran thread, moderated by a falling volatility index and a modest 0.66% realised cash range. Confidence at 87 reflects verified current levels for the cash index, index futures, the broad market index, the semiconductor index, the volatility index, four Treasury points and both crude benchmarks, a primary-source macro release, verified reporting of the UN remarks, and fresh supplementary cross-asset context; the deduction covers the blocked live blogs, the partial shared context and the fact that tick-level pullback depth is not directly observable.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours contain a complete set of 24 published hourly assessments, none of them revised with later information. Monday's U.S. session carried the highest readings of the window: Tail built from 28 at 15:00 UTC to a 33 peak with Stress 57 in the 19:00 UTC power hour, and every hour from 15:00 to 19:00 UTC mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES as the index trended to a record close. After the cash close the characterisation decayed quickly, with Tail falling to 23 by 20:00 UTC and 14 by 21:00 UTC. The entire Asian and European overnight then held an 11-13 Tail band with Stress between 32 and 39 and Confidence between 85 and 87, mapping to EA_ON throughout. The final two hours mark today's U.S. session: 13:00 UTC carried Tail 13 with Stress 43, and 14:00 UTC stepped up to Tail 21 with Stress 46 and a trend-up characterisation on observed post-open continuation, the reading this assessment revises on the subsequent rejection of the session high.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps Tail inside an 11-21 band and no forecast hour reaches the block threshold. The remaining U.S. cash hours rise modestly from 17 to 19 across the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction and Barkin remarks, then peak at 21 in the 19:00 UTC power hour, the only slot that maps to WATCH and the same hour that carried Monday's highest reading. From the 20:00 UTC cash close the path assumes liquidity drains and the directional characterisation loses definition, exactly as it did after Monday's close: Tail falls to 16, then 13, and settles onto an 11-12 overnight floor that mirrors the band actually observed through the previous night. It rebuilds gradually from the 07:00 UTC European open, reaching 14 by 12:00 UTC and then 17 and 18 in the final two hours, which contain Wednesday's cash open at 13:30 UTC, the high-impact S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC and the immediate post-release digestion. No later hour is scored on observed structure, because pre-event alignment is not counted as already observed and no future price path is visible from this cutoff; Confidence therefore decays steadily from 87 to 65 across the window.
